summary: The agenda for the May 1971 Network Working Group meeting, from May 16 through the evening of May 19 at the Dennis Hotel in Atlantic City. It gives the room names and the daily schedule of sessions. RFC 149 later changed it a little.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC publishes the schedule for a Network Working Group meeting in May 1971. It lists session topics, times, rooms and suggested RFCs to read in advance.

sections.title: Meeting Dates and Rooms
sections.content:
The meeting runs from Sunday evening, May 16, through Wednesday evening, May 19. Most sessions are in the Wicker Room at the Dennis Hotel, while the Sunday evening meeting is in the Royal Box Room.

Morning sessions start at 9 a.m., afternoon sessions at 1:30 p.m. and evening sessions at 8 p.m. The Wicker Room is reserved for private meetings at other times through Thursday afternoon.
sections.plainLanguage: The agenda gives the meeting dates, room names and standard start times. It also says when attendees can use the main room for private meetings.

sections.title: Reports and Technical Sessions
sections.content:
Sunday evening is for short reports from hosts and committees. Monday morning covers the Network Information Center and the Telnet committee's proposed protocol. Monday afternoon covers file transfer, the Terminal IMP, network management and other ARPA projects.

Monday evening is about operating systems and networks. Tuesday morning covers the proposed data reconfiguration service and data management systems. The listed sessions include presentations and discussion of current work.
sections.plainLanguage: The first sessions cover site reports, Telnet, file transfer, network planning, operating systems and data management.

sections.title: Remaining Technical and Organizational Topics
sections.content:
Tuesday evening is scheduled for socket numbers, procedures for testing NCPs and Telnets, protocol experiments, the initial connection protocol and remaining Host/Host protocol issues.

Wednesday evening addresses non-technical matters. The agenda says the Network Working Group had grown and changed and would discuss its organization, goals for the end of 1971 and steps to reach them.
sections.plainLanguage: The final sessions cover unresolved protocol work and how the Network Working Group should organize itself.
